findings: src/game.js: With AI off, place computer at (17.6,0,180) and player at (18.8,3,270), then hold W for 1 second: collision resolution moves the stationary computer instead of stopping the player at contact.

src/game.js: With AI off, place computer at (0,0) and player at (-5,1.449,0), fire and step 0.5 seconds: endpoint-only collision checks miss the shell touching the computer, leaving its health at 100 instead of 75.

src/ai.js:31-36 checks visibility toward the player's centre instead of the actual firing heading, so a stationary player at (-15,-6) remains unharmed after 60 seconds while the computer repeatedly shoots into an inner wall.
src/game.js:90-94 checks only shell endpoints against walls, so firing from (-8.049759197546795,-3.6102408024532053) at heading 315 passes through an inner-wall corner without bouncing.
src/game.js:84 excludes exact contact, so firing from (-5,1.45) at heading 0 past a computer at (0,0) leaves its health at 100 although the shell touches it.

src/tools.js:31 rounds each step duration independently, so 100 valid calls with seconds=0.01 advance 1.667 seconds and move a forward-driving tank 10 units instead of the requested 1 second and 6 units.

src/ai.js rejects every waypoint when the computer starts inside a wall's inflated planning bounds, so valid placements at computer (-10.3, -8) and player (-5, -8) leave it stationary without firing for 30 seconds.
src/arena.js rejects the legal wall-contact placement (-10.2, -8) because floating-point rounding makes its computed wall distance slightly less than the tank's radius.
